\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = \frac{1}{n^2} \sum_{j=-r}^{r} \sum_{i=-r}^{r} I(x+i,\, y+j),
\qquad
n = 3,
\quad
r = \frac{n-1}{2}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value
- \((x, y)\): Pixel position. x grows to the right and y grows downward.
- \(n\): Window width in pixels. It is odd.
- \(r\): Window radius in pixels

Each output pixel is the mean of the n by n window around it. Every weight is 1 / n^2, so the weights add up to 1. The kernel is the outer product of two 1D means, so the filter runs as a mean along rows and then a mean along columns.
